newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FORECAST--CITIC Pac '96 net seen doubled.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--CITIC Pac '96 net seen doubled.

text.p: Exceptionals are seen brightening CITIC Pacific Ltd's 1996 net profit, with increased contributions from infrastructure projects and a turnaround by its trading arm adding highlights, analysts said on Monday.
"CITIC Pacific was the outperformer of the sector, not in stock price but in business in 1996," said Dennis Leung at Dharmala Securities.
Analysts estimate the China-backed conglomerate will report net profit of between HK$6.38 billion and HK$6.99 billion, up 108 to 127 percent from 1995, at Thursday's announcement.

In its 1996 first-half results, CITIC Pacific reported an exceptional profit of HK$3.3 billion from the disposal of a 3.85 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and a 17.66 percent interest in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd.
"Stripping out exceptionals, net will be HK$3.58 billion," said Anil Daswani, an analyst at Salomon Brothers.
Underlying growth will come from increased contributions from China infrastructure projects and solid growth in CITIC Pacific's trading arm Dah Chong Hong (DCH), he said.
"It's not really a rebound but we are looking for sharp growth coming through from DCH," Daswani said.
Demands for motor vehicles was turning around and the weakening yen boosting margins substantially, he added.
Dah Chong Hong profits fell 35 percent in 1995, mainly hit by the weak motor sales in China and Hong Kong markets.
Dharmala's Leung said the growth in food and cosmetic trading also should have boosted profits in Dah Chong Hong.
Daswani expected Dah Chong Hong to make a profit of HK$504 million in 1996 against HK$462 million in 1995.

But the largest chunk of CITIC Pacific's profits should come from Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd after CITIC Pacific raise it stake in the Hong Kong flag carrier to 25 percent from 10 percent in mid-1996, he said.
Salomon saw Cathay contributing about HK$828 million of CITIC Pacific's pre-tax profit for last year.
The effect of selling down the Hongkong Telecom stake to about eight percent would be partly offset by the increase of its Cathay Pacific holdings, analysts said.

"Associate profits are expected to be slightly down on last year at HK$2.6 billion due to the timing of CITIC's sell down of Hongkong Telecom and its increased stake in Cathay Pacific," ING Barings' Mark Simpson said in a recent report.
Property investment and development were expected to account for about HK$180 million and HK$170 million, respectively, Leung said.

Analysts generally expected exceptional items would continue to be a significant factor in the company's profit this year since CITIC Pacific might tempted to sell off its remaining interest in Hongkkong Telecom.
They were also looking for contributions to come from new 20-percent associate China Light & Power Ltd this and next years.
